questions.stem: An 88-year-old male with dementia is brought from an old-age home with reports of “coffee-ground vomitus”. He does not seem to have abdominal pain and is not actively vomiting. Rectal exam shows stool-positive for occult blood. His Hb was 8.5mg/dl . He is hemodynamically stable. What is the best management for this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: IV access, type and screen, IV PPI, admit to the hospital

options.label: B
options.text: IV access, CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis

options.label: C
options.text: Zofran ODT, oral PPI, discharge back to the nursing home

options.label: D
options.text: IV fluid bolus, IV PPI, discharge back to the nursing home
